CARDIOVASCULAR

◉   What You See

Bundles of cardiac muscle viewed at low magnification. The section demonstrates the thick muscular wall of the heart and the organization of myocardial tissue.

⚙   What It Means

Cardiac muscle is specialized for continuous, coordinated contraction. At higher magnification, cardiomyocytes show central nuclei, branching fibres and intercalated discs.

▥   Why It Matters

Recognizing the organization of myocardium helps connect cardiac structure with pumping function and provides a baseline for identifying pathological change.

SLIDE BOX GUIDE

How to Use the Slide Box

A quick guide to exploring, zooming, labelling, and studying virtual histology slides.

1

Choose a tissue system

Start from Tissues and select an organ system such as Cardiovascular or Respiratory.

2

Open a slide

Select a slide to open the virtual viewer. The image can be explored without leaving the Slide Box.

3

Zoom in and out

Use + and −, your mouse wheel/trackpad, or double-click directly on the image.

4

Pan around the tissue

When zoomed in, click and drag the slide to move around the tissue and inspect different regions.

5

Switch views

Use Unlabelled to test yourself, then switch to Labelled to check important structures.

6

Reset your view

Click Reset View whenever you want to return to the full-slide view.

✦

Study tip

Try identifying the tissue on the unlabelled view first. Zoom into areas of interest, make your identification, then switch to the labelled view to check your answer.
